correctness.rationale: Equal determinants force the normalized symmetric matrix C to have trace zero and eigenvalues ±s. Its lens is exactly norm-square plus s times an absolute quadratic term, invariant under square symmetries. Uniqueness of global John/Löwner ellipses makes them centered disks, and the radial extremes plus four-point isotropic contacts determine them. Exact determinant algebra yields the mismatch, area ratio and inverse. A standalone checker completed 187 actual positive-definite pairs; the analytic proof supplies continuum validity.

Full texts of Kahan and Seeger and both closest published equal-area ellipse results do not state the exact joint John–Löwner homothety and spectral inverse ratio. Actual semantic and general-web searches were made, with a concrete residual risk of unindexed or implicit optimization coverage. The general symmetric planar factor-two bound is classical; only the exact strict ratio and inverse profile are new here.

value.rationale: The equal-area lens is a canonical affine-invariant convex body. The exact optimal inscribed and enclosing ellipses unexpectedly share shape for every nonaligned pair, and their ratio is a strict sharp 1-to-2 spectral mismatch signature that reconstructs the input affine class. It is a complete motivated classification with contact certificates and equality/degeneration thresholds, not a table recomputation or arbitrary parameter slice.
